([[Los Angeles, California]]) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] (1997–2001) | draft_year = 2001 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 52 | draft_team = [[Utah Jazz]] | career_start = 2001 | career_end = 2011 | career_position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | career_number = 31, 20 | coach_start = 2014 | years1 = {{nbay|2001|start}}–{{nbay|2008|end}} | team1 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years2 = {{nbay|2009|full=y}} | team2 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years3 = {{nbay|2010|end}} | team3 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2010|end}} | team4 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | cyears1 = {{nbay|2014|start}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | cteam1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] (assistant) | cyears2 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | cteam2 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] (assistant) | highlights = '''As player:''' * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] ([[2000–01 Pacific-10 Conference men's basketball season|2001]]) * Fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (1997) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[1997 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|1997]]) '''As assistant coach:''' * 3× [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ({{nbafy|2015}}, {{nbafy|2017}}, {{nbafy|2018}}) | stats_league = NBA | stat1label = [[Point (basketball)|Points]] | stat1value = 2,095 (3.9 ppg) | stat2label = [[Rebound (basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = 1,579 (2.9 rpg) | stat3label = [[Block (basketball)|Blocks]] | stat3value = 98 (0.2 bpg) }} '''Jarron Thomas Collins''' (born December 2, 1978) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is an assistant coach for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected in the second round of the [[2001 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]], and played 10 seasons in the NBA. His twin brother, [[Jason Collins|Jason]], also played in the league. ==Early life== Jarron Collins was born in [[Northridge, California]].{{cite web|title=Jarron Collins|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/988/jarron-collins|publisher=ESPN|access-date=December 19, 2011}} He and his twin brother [[Jason Collins|Jason]], who also became an NBA player, graduated from [[Harvard-Westlake School]] in [[Los Angeles]], California. Also on the team was actor [[Jason Segel]], who starred in a slam dunk contest after Collins deferred to allow his teammate to participate.{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1996-03-02-sp-42245-story.html | work=Los Angeles Times | first=Vince | last=Kowalick | title=Twin-Engine Props | date=March 2, 1996}} Collins shot 72 percent from the floor and averaged 13.8 points and 9.2 rebounds during his senior year in high school.{{cite web|url=http://www.gostanford.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/collins_jarron00.html |title=Jarron Collins |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=2009-09-23 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711113725/http://www.gostanford.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/collins_jarron00.html |archive-date=2011-07-11 }} ==College career== Collins attended [[Stanford University]], where he was a two-time [[All-America]]n and finished his Stanford career in the top ten all time in four career categories: rebounds, blocked shots, field-goal percentage and games played.{{cite web|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/stan/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/0809-m-baskbl-mg-10.pdf|title=Stanford Men's Basketball Media Guide|publisher=Stanford University|year=2009|access-date=2009-09-23|archive-date=2012-11-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121112084126/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/stan/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/0809-m-baskbl-mg-10.pdf|url-status=dead}} He was also recruited by [[UCLA Bruins basketball|UCLA]], where he, his brother, and [[Earl Watson]] were the guests at the recruiting dinner that led to the firing of [[Jim Harrick]] at UCLA.{{cite news|last=Saxon |first=Lisa |url=http://www.press-enterprise.com/newsarchive/2001/03/01/983425572.html |title=The meal heard 'round the Pac-10 |publisher=Press-Enterprise |date=March 1, 2001 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928021510/http://www.press-enterprise.com/newsarchive/2001/03/01/983425572.html |archive-date=September 28, 2007 }} ==NBA career== [[File:Jarron Collins PHX.jpg|thumb|right|Collins with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2009]] Collins was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round of the [[2001 NBA draft]] and played eight seasons with the Jazz until becoming a free agent following the 2009 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sltrib.com/Sports/ci_13398314|title=Collins gone; Harpring too?|date=September 23, 2009|work=[[Salt Lake Tribune]]|last=Siler|first=Ross|access-date=2009-09-23|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005063026/http://www.sltrib.com/Sports/ci_13398314|archive-date=October 5, 2012}} Collins spent the 2009 NBA preseason with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He was waived by Portland, but then claimed off waivers by the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4930 |title=Suns get rights to Jarron Collins |work=InsideHoops.com |date=October 26, 2009 |access-date=May 8, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221220058/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4930 |archive-date=December 21, 2016 |url-status=dead }} Collins later joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], signing a 10-day contract on January 7, 2011. He renewed his tenure, later signing another 10-day contract on January 17, 2011. On March 1, 2011, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]],{{cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2011/03/trail_blazers_sign_jarron_coll.html|title= Trail Blazers sign Jarron Collins to add depth at center|publisher=OregonLive.com|date=March 1, 2011|access-date=March 1, 2011}} and was released after finishing a second ten-day contract. That second 10-day contract ended up being Collins' final days in the NBA, as his final game was on March 17, 2011, in a 111 - 70 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers. In his final game, Collins played for 4 minutes and recorded no stats. He retired from basketball after the season.{{cite news |last=Golliver |first=Ben |title=Jason Collins reveals that he is gay |date=April 29, 2013 |work=SI.com |url=http://nba.si.com/2013/04/29/jason-collins-comes-out-openly-gay-male-athlete-wizards-david-stern-arn-tellem-ernie-grunfeld/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501123709/http://nba.si.com/2013/04/29/jason-collins-comes-out-openly-gay-male-athlete-wizards-david-stern-arn-tellem-ernie-grunfeld/ |archive-date=2013-05-01 |url-status=dead }} ==Post-playing career== In 2013, he was working for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] as a scout.[http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/jason-collins-openly-gay-and-still-unsigned-waits-and-wonders-20131012-2ven2.html Jason Collins, openly gay and still unsigned, waits and wonders] He later worked as a college basketball analyst for [[Pac-12 Network]]s.{{cite news |url=http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/blogstv/56987129-63/pac-basketball-networks-season.html.csp |title=Ex-Jazzman Jarron Collins joins Pac-12 Networks |date=October 11, 2013 |work=[[Salt Lake Tribune]] |last=Pierce| first=Scott}} On July 3, 2014, Collins joined [[Steve Kerr]]'s staff as a player development coach for the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web |date=July 3, 2014 |title=Warriors Announce Steve Kerr's Coaching Staff |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-announce-steve-kerrs-coaching-staff |access-date=July 3, 2014 |website=NBA.com}} Collins won his first championship when the Warriors defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2015 NBA Finals]]. On July 29, 2015, he was promoted to assistant coach by the Warriors.{{cite web |date=July 29, 2015 |title=Warriors Announce Coaching Staff for 2015-16 Season |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-announce-coaching-staff-2015-16-season |access-date=July 29, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} Collins won his second championship in three years when the Warriors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers in the [[2017 NBA Finals]]. Collins won his third championship in four years when the Warriors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers in the [[2018 NBA Finals]]. In June 2021, Collins and the Warriors mutually agreed to part ways.{{cite web|last=Spears|first=Marc J.|title=Assistant coach Jarron Collins moving on from Golden State Warriors, eyes head-coaching job|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31584971/assistant-coach-jarron-collins-moving-golden-state-warriors-eyes-head-coaching-job|work=ESPN.com|date=June 7, 2021|access-date=June 7, 2021}}{{cite news|first=Monte|last=Poole|title=Why the time was right for Collins to leave Warriors|date=June 9, 2021|website=NBCSports.com|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/why-jarron-collins-leaving-warriors-feels-right-move-now|access-date=July 28, 2021}} On August 4, 2021, Collins was hired as assistant coach by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |date=August 4, 2021 |title=Pelicans announce coaching staff |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-announce-coaching-staff-jarron-collins-mike-dantoni-080421 |access-date=August 4, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player
